title: Release Ops scripting and calendar scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for the upcoming September release lane — focusing on three things we keep getting asked for: 1) compact release-day scripts (one-liners + failure cases), 2) a compact week-by-week calendar for the rollout window, and 3) a short, editable release-notes draft we can paste into the release ticket.

TL;DR goals:
- Keep window to 72 hours (soft) with a 48h hotfix guardrail.
- Provide operator one-liners for common tasks (scale up/down, model swap, route fallback).
- Define 4 observability signals as primary SLOs for go/no-go checks.
- Draft release notes in plain language + tech bullet list.

Quick calendar (week-of view) — Sep 8 release lane (example):
- Mon Sep 8: Preflight window 09:00–17:00 PT
  - Run smoke-suite v2 (see script below)
  - Dry-run model swap in staging; validate KV-cache integrity
  - Confirm rollout groups / canary buckets in feature-flag UI
  - Slack ping @oncall-release 14:00 PT for go/no-go
- Tue Sep 9: Canary day 1 (target 1% traffic 10:00–16:00 PT)
  - Observe latency P50/P95, E2E errors, tail latency spikes
  - If errors > 0.5% or P95 > 600ms -> rollback plan (see matrix)
- Wed Sep 10: Canary day 2 (ramp to 10% if stable)
  - Final rollout decision at 15:00 PT
  - Begin staged ramp to 50% and then to 100% overnight if unchanged

Operator scripts (one-liners) — Appendix A
- Scale pool up (adds 2 nodes): 
  kubectl scale deploy/release-gpu-pool --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy/release-gpu-pool -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+2)) 
  # verify pods Ready within 6m: kubectl get pods -l app=release-gpu-pool -w

- Swap model alias to fallback variant (instant):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://console.redwood/api/v1/model-alias/swap -d '{"alias":"prod-textgen","to":"prod-textgen-quant-fallback"}'
  # wait 10s and check health: curl -sS https://console.redwood/health/model/prod-textgen || echo 'health fail'

- Throttle route to safety lane (quickly drop new traffic):
  curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/v1/routing/throttle -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","throttle_pct":10,"reason":"rollout-safety"}'

Primary observability signals (pick 4) — Appendix B
- S1: Service error rate (5xx) across the model route — threshold 0.5% (rolling 5m)
- S2: P95 latency for token generation (model endpoint) — threshold 600ms
- S3: Client-side end-to-end user errors (frankly from product telemetry) — >0.3% triggers investigation
- S4: Queue depth/backpressure metric on ingress queue — >30% sustained -> slow ramp or rollback

Decision matrix (simplified):
- Block and rollback immediately if: S1 > 1% OR S2 > 1s OR S3 > 1% 
- Pause and investigate if: S1 between 0.5%–1% OR S2 between 600ms–1s OR S4 > 30%
- Continue ramp if all S1–S4 < threshold for 30m window

Rollback matrix (fast paths):
- If model variant fails (errors/quality regressions): swap alias back to previous stable tag (one-liner above) and mark incident in Jira JIRA-RELEASE-789-ROLLBACK
- If infra pressure (GPU OOMs / pod crashes): scale down new pool and route to stable cluster; notify SRE immediately

Smoke suite (commands we run in preflight):
- smoke/run_smoke.sh --suite=all --parallel=4 --check=kv-cache,kv-prefix-cache,latency,embed-consistency
- smoke/check_logs.sh --since="1h" --grep=OOM

Release notes (editable draft) — short & product-friendly:
Title: September inference platform rollout: model swap, routing improvements, and stability fixes
Summary (1–2 sentence):
We are rolling out a staged update to the text generation pipeline that includes a guarded model swap (quantized fallback variant), routing throttles for high-load scenarios, and several operator tooling improvements to reduce failover time. Users should see similar latency for typical queries and fewer failover interruptions.
Technical bullets (for release ticket):
- Swapped prod-textgen -> prod-textgen-quant (fallback path remains available)
- Introduced route-level throttling and fast safety lane to protect downstream services
- Improved autoscaling script to detect KV-cache pressure and pre-warm nodes
- Fixed a regression in the streaming proxy that could cause 5xx under long-tail requests
Known issues / caveats:
- Very long context (>8k tokens) may still see slight increases in latency during ramp; we are monitoring
- Beta customers on dedicated pools may need their routing updated (SEs notified)

Open questions / TODOs:
- (Marco) confirm that feature-flag groups are configured for customer cohorts A/B/C — ticket: FF-342
- (Claire) produce a short postmortem template we can attach if rollback occurs
- (Samir) verify that probe frequency for model health isn't throttled behind our RL proxy (observability tweak)
- Add a short troubleshooting FAQ to the release ticket for SEs.

Post-release quick checks (first 6 hours):
- 0–30m: confirm no immediate 5xx spike and P95 within threshold (S1/S2)
- 30–120m: check error patterns, tail latencies, and queue depth; verify cache hit rates
- 120–360m: customer-facing metrics (product telemetry) show no regression on baseline queries

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the scripts in github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts in sync — prefer small, idempotent ops; avoid big DB migrations in this lane
- If we need to pause, aim for a 1h decision loop: pause -> triage (30m) -> decide -> act. Communicate via slack:#release-ops with a pinned summary message.

Appendix: handy links (quick copy/paste)
- Release ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/JIRA-RELEASE-789
- Release scripts PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts/pull/432
- Operator runbook (canonical): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Operator+Runbook

End of scratchpad — drop notes below as you test, we'll tighten and move to "release-briefing" once stable.
